name: MiniCPM-V-4_5
notes: TWO-PART MODEL, and the small-but-capable positioning is a deliberate architecture choice, not just a size claim. (1) Vision: SigLIP, 27 layers, hidden 1152, 16 heads, patch 14, image_size 980 (note: 980, not 384 or 896 -- a large native input), batch_vision_input true. TILING + RESAMPLER: slice_mode true, slice_config.max_slice_nums 9, patch_size 14, and the decisive field query_num 64 -- a PERCEIVER-STYLE RESAMPLER that compresses every 448 slice down to 64 tokens (image_size 448 at top level, batch_3d_resampler true for video). VISION TOKENS: 64 per slice + 64 for the global view, so 128 tokens for a small image and up to 10 * 64 = 640 tokens at max_slice_nums 9. DOMINANCE: TEXT DOMINATES at default settings (128-640 vision tokens vs a text prompt), and vision stays bounded even at max tiling because the resampler caps per-slice cost. That bound is the whole design: MiniCPM pays for resolution inside the ViT (batch_vision_input) but caps what reaches the LLM. Cheapest vision-token path in this slice among the high-capability models. (2) LLM: dense decoder, 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 (stated explicitly), intermediate 12288, vocab 151,748, max_position 40,960, rope_theta 1e6, use_sliding_window false. ARCHITECTURE = dense. No positional scaling applied (rope_scaling null). KV CACHE: 36 * 8 * 128 * 2 * 2 = 147,456 B/token (144 KiB). At 40,960 ctx that is 5.6 GiB per sequence at bf16 -- a far more honest serving figure than the 131k-262k contexts some siblings record, because 40,960 is what this model actually declares. params_b 8.696 = HF API safetensors total (8,695,895,280).
